IICB(Glc), the membrane subunit of the glucose transporter, forms a homotrimeric structure with a molecular weight of about 100 kDa.

IICB(Glc), the membrane subunit of the glucose transporter of the phosphotransfer system, is an integral membrane protein that forms dimers and is capable of forming small 2D crystalline lattices in lipid bilayers.
IICB(Glc), the membrane subunit of the bacterial phosphoenolpyruvate:sugar phosphotransferasesystem, is a dimer in the native state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IICB(Glc), the transmembrane component of the glucose transporter, is an integral protein that is organized into dimers in the cytoplasmically exposed part of the membrane.
IICB(Glc), which has an apparent molecular weight of 50 kDa, is a trimeric protein consisting of two identical 25-kDa subunits and a third 20-kDa subunit.
the glucose transporter consists of two subunits, IIA(Glc), a dimer of about 40 kDa, and IICB(Glc), a trimer of about 100 kDa, with a stoichiometry of 1:1.

the glucose permease of the phosphotransfer system can be purified to homogeneity and reconstituted in lipid membranes to yield well-defined structures that can be analyzed by cryo-electron microscopy and image processing.
IICB(Glc), a 14.5 kDa integral membrane protein, forms dimers in the membrane and that this dimeric structure is preserved upon reconstitution.
